If it does not publish tenders on its own site, the only routes are EKR/KBA filings (if it is an ajánlatkérő) and trade-press/vendor announcements, which changes the collection design substantially.

brief: Hungary's state-owned and state-influenced financial buyers publish on three overlapping layers: their own statutory 'közérdekű adatok / gazdálkodási adatok' disclosure pages (MNB, MFB, EXIM, Diákhitel, KELER, Kincstár), the national EKR platform plus the Közbeszerzési Értesítő/KBA gazette, and TED for above-threshold procedures — with Magyar Posta additionally running a genuine supplier-facing tender page whose documentation is gated behind SAP Ariba. The highest-value payments infrastructure buyer, GIRO Zrt. (BKR/AFR operator, MNB-owned), appears to publish no tender page of its own, so its vendor pipeline must be inferred from EKR filings, business rules and trade-press reporting. A structural complication is DKÜ (Korm. rendelet 301/2018), the central purchasing body that absorbs much government-sector IT procurement into framework agreements, meaning buyer-name-filtered feeds will under-count unless DKÜ frameworks are tracked in parallel. All meaningful content is Hungarian-language; English surfaces exist only on TED and partial EXIM/EN pages and should never be the primary collection route.
